data.hypothesis: Replacing the modulo/shared-memory reduction tree with five warp-shuffle steps per warp and a four-warp combine may reduce block-local overhead while retaining the 128-element tile and recursive host stages. Unsigned modulo-2^32 partial sums preserve the final exact result when it fits int32; the replacement conversion stores each partial's bit pattern without an out-of-range signed cast. This is a hypothesis, not evidence that local reduction is the bottleneck.
data.notes: The supplied h01 development attempt failed to build because __uint_as_int was undefined; this proposal replaces it with an in-range signed conversion that preserves the 32-bit pattern. Only the baseline has official results so far: correct on all 10 supplied cases (n=1, 127, 1024, 65536, and 4194304; seeds 23 and 60). Its repeated full-program timings were 46.5651, 46.0806, and 46.0864 microseconds (mean 46.2441 microseconds). This candidate has not yet been built, correctness-tested, or timed; no candidate timing or speedup is claimed.
transformations: Retain 128-thread blocks and recursive host-stage launches, but perform a warp shuffle reduction first and combine the four warp totals through shared memory and a second warp reduction.
Use unsigned modulo-2^32 additions for partial sums, then map each unsigned bit pattern to int using only in-range signed conversions.
